note: Loa means a speaker or loudspeaker generally. Loa phóng thanh cầm tay specifies the portable hand-held voice-amplifying device.
面白い directly includes amusing and funny, and is a natural equivalent for entertaining in this adjective sense.
努めて has a direct diligently sense in JMdict; its effortful nuance matches doing something with appropriate effort.
恋する is the natural Japanese verb for being in love with or falling in love with someone, despite the English expression having a different part of speech.
励ます includes encouraging or cheering someone up, which matches making a person happier or less downcast in this transitive sense.
罪を犯す means commit a crime or sin, and phạm tội is the standard Vietnamese verb for committing a sin as well as an offense.
可能性 means possibility broadly. 確率 specifically means probability or likelihood in JMdict (ent_seq 1205950 sense 0).
悪口 covers speaking ill generally. 罵倒 is a closer term for verbal abuse or vilification and is listed in JMdict (ent_seq 1471540 sense 0).
遅滞 and trì hoãn can mean delay generally. 先延ばし is glossed procrastination in JMdict (ent_seq 2098630 sense 0), while thói trì hoãn captures habitual postponing.
日焼け commonly names sunburn in context, and cháy nắng directly means a burn caused by sunlight; the English definition selects the burn reading.
Chuyên viên quay phim is correct but formal and suggests a specialist. Người quay phim is a more natural neutral Vietnamese term for someone operating a movie or television camera.
踏む and giẫm can mean a neutral step on. 踏みにじる means trample or crush underfoot in JMdict (ent_seq 1450260 sense 0), and giẫm đạp better conveys the forceful action.
蝶々 is a common, slightly informal word for butterfly, and bướm is the standard Vietnamese equivalent in this insect sense.
知り合う and làm quen naturally express becoming acquainted with someone; the definition explicitly includes meeting a person.
うさぎ and thỏ are the ordinary equivalents for rabbit. Their wider dictionary coverage of hare does not prevent the intended rabbit reading here.
対話 means dialogue or conversation, and sự hội thoại is correct Vietnamese, though somewhat formal.
視野 and trường thị giác both name the visual field; the Vietnamese term is technical but precise for the stated definition.
Sự liên đới is valid but formal and legalistic. Tình đoàn kết is the more natural Vietnamese expression for mutual solidarity around a shared goal.
Vũ công usually implies a professional dancer. Người nhảy múa is a descriptive neutral term that also includes someone dancing as a hobby.
Cúi means bend down generally. Cúi chào specifies bending as a greeting or gesture of respect, matching bow in this sense.
鎧 refers mainly to body armor. 装甲 means armor or armoring in JMdict (ent_seq 1402300 sense 0) and better covers protective layers on vehicles and other objects.
Người máy means a robot generally. Người máy hình người specifies the human-like design that distinguishes an android.
とうもろこし and ngô both name maize (Zea mays); ngô is standard in northern Vietnam, with bắp common in the south.
Vực means an abyss or chasm more generally. Hẻm núi is the Vietnamese term for a narrow, steep-sided valley cut by a river.
くじら and cá voi usually exclude dolphins and porpoises. 鯨類 is glossed as cetaceans in JMdict (ent_seq 2167570 sense 0), and bộ cá voi names the full taxonomic order in Vietnamese.
紛らわしい means confusing because something can be mistaken for something else. 分かりにくい means hard to understand in JMdict (ent_seq 1606540 sense 0), matching the stated lack of clarity or order.
潜水艦 is the standard Japanese word for submarine, and tàu ngầm is the standard Vietnamese term; the simple English definition does not exclude military craft.
In Japanese food contexts かに can refer to crab served as food. The Vietnamese cua names the animal more generally, while thịt cua specifies its flesh as food.
Vận động viên is gender-neutral. Vận động viên nam preserves the male-specific meaning in the English definition.
Cành means branch generally. Cành nhỏ specifies the small, thin branch described by twig.
Sự ghét is an awkward literal nominalization. Sự căm ghét is a natural Vietnamese noun for intense dislike or hatred.
渦 includes a swirl or eddy in air or water, which matches a current turning back or against the main current in the stated definition.
クラクション is the standard Japanese car horn, and còi is a natural Vietnamese horn term within the English alarm-or-automobile-horn sense.
夕方 includes early evening and dusk, matching the English definition that explicitly includes both the time period and dusk.
他人 is glossed as outsider or stranger in JMdict and fits the supplied outsider; stranger sense.
招待状 and giấy mời specifically denote written invitations. 招待 is the general invitation noun in JMdict (ent_seq 1349610 sense 0), and lời mời can be a verbal or written invitation.
被験者 is limited to a human test subject. 研究対象 means subject of research in JMdict (ent_seq 2642470 sense 0) and includes animals or inanimate objects under study.
Bộ phận rời is understandable but descriptive and can imply detachability. Mô đun is the common Vietnamese technical term for a self-contained system component.
Chào can mean either hello or goodbye. Tạm biệt is an unambiguous Vietnamese parting expression corresponding to bye.
咬傷 and vết cắn both name a wound left by a bite; the Japanese term is formal or technical but semantically exact.
